headline: Monday absorbed the oil gap without an equity move and paid for it in rate vol. Futures are collecting the bill pre-market.
stance: The tell was not the yield, it was what the market paid for optionality around a meeting fifteen days out while the front end sat perfectly still. Equities deferred their reaction by a session and are taking it before the open, into the first data the new stance has to survive.

news.head: Futures take the session equities declined to have
news.body: S&P 500 -0.57%, Nasdaq 100 -1.02%, Russell 2000 -0.48%, VIX 15.79 (~5am ET). Monday's cash close barely registered it.

news.head: Crude holds the war premium into a second session
news.body: WTI $87.75, +2.3%, Brent near $90 (~5am ET). A gap that has not faded by the second morning stops being a headline and starts being supply.

news.head: Gold gives back Monday and more
news.body: $4,423, -1.3% (~5am ET), through Friday's close too. Gold vol has been coming in alongside it, so this is an orderly exit from length, not a liquidation.

implications: Rate vol repriced without the yield moving. That is a market paying for a two-sided meeting, not a new level — it argues for the range break over the direction.
Every stretched position in the data is a long that has been in place for weeks. A hawkish print at ten hurts commodities and the belly of the curve, not equity hedges.

watch.head: ISM manufacturing and job openings, 10am ET
watch.body: Quits ran 2.0% in June. Openings is the half that can still argue the labour side against September; the factory survey mostly cannot.

watch.head: Payrolls Friday, CPI the 11th, FOMC the 16th
watch.body: Three prints and fifteen days. What the market paid for rate vol on Monday says it does not plan to sit still between them.

watch.head: First clean funding marks since the turn
watch.body: Month end cleared with the facility barely touched and no strain in the plumbing. Today's fixing is the first read on the other side of it.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: The move since Friday went into rate vol, not into the yield. The front end did not budge on Monday and the market still paid up for optionality into the meeting.
The long end added a fourth straight session regardless. Friday's repricing was about the meeting; the 20s and 30s have their own problem and it has not gone away.
So the curve steepened with the 2-year pinned, all of it from the back. A supply steepener, not a Fed one, and the two want opposite trades.
sections.positioning: The 5-year is the one that moved: spec length added seven percentile points on the week to a three-year maximum, joining the 2-year. Length is migrating out the curve.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: The index move was nothing on Monday and the internals were not. The share of S&P names above their 50-day has fallen three straight sessions, to exactly half.
The 200-day count fell the same three sessions. When both go down together it is not rotation between names, it is the participation base itself shrinking.
Front-month vol finally caught a bid against three-month, the first move up in the term structure in a week. Still steeply contango, so the hedge is not expensive yet.
sections.positioning: Russell 2000 spec length has sat at the 2nd percentile of three years for eighteen weeks. Small caps are the one place with no length left to unwind if today lands hawkish.

single_name.note: Funko - new to the screen today, insider buy filed Aug 26, trading above its 200-day. Only 2.8 days to cover, so the signal is the buyer, not a squeeze.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: The one daily credit read available fell a fourth straight session while the cash spread marks still carry Friday's tights. The proxy is leaking ahead of the marks.
Those cash marks are stale as of Friday. Nothing in them has seen the oil gap, Monday's rate-vol move, or this morning's futures.
sections.positioning: Primary-dealer high-yield inventory fell six points on the week to the 6th percentile of three years. Dealers are carrying less into payrolls than they took into month end.

ideas.line: 4 open · 0 closed — no hit rate until 10 (too few to mean anything)
